chunks: And also, Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Yahya from Hariz from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A slave woman escaped from her masters and went to a tribe other than her own tribe, and claimed that she was free. At that time, a man married her. Later, her masters captured her, and she had already given birth to children. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the husband establishes proof that he married her on the basis that she was free, her children are freed, and the people take their slave woman. And if he does not establish proof, his back is beaten (for receiving the penalty of false claim) and her children are enslaved.'

key_terms.أَوْجِعَ ظَهْرُهُ: His back was beaten (receiving the penalty of false claim)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the children of a slave woman who claims freedom and marries before being recaptured?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the juristic outcome for a runaway slave woman who marries under the assumption of freedom, highlighting the Shia legal principle of *Umm al-Walad* (mother of a child) where paternity establishes emancipation for offspring if the husband proves her free status at the time of marriage. The ruling underscores the importance of evidentiary standards in family law, distinguishing between cases where the husband acts in good faith versus those where he does not, thereby determining whether the children inherit their mother's status or remain enslaved.
